en: The Hymn to the Eighteen Seats of Power (Śaktipīṭhas)
The goddess Śāṅkarī is in Laṅkā; Kāmākṣī is in the city of Kāñcī;
Śṛṅkhalādevī is in Pradyumna; and Cāmuṇḍī is in Krauñcapaṭṭana.
Jogulāmbā is at Alampur; Bhramarāmbikā is on Śrīśaila; Mahālakṣmī is at Kolhāpur; and Ekavīrikā is at Māhūr.
Mahākālī is in Ujjayinī, Puruhūtikā is on the Pīṭhikā,
Girijā-devī is in Oḍhyā, and [the goddess] Māṇikyā is in Dakṣavāṭaka.
At Harikṣetra she is Kāmarūpā; at Prayāga she is Mādhaveśvarī;
at Jvālā she is the goddess Vaiṣṇavī; and at Gayā she is Māṅgalyagaurikā.
Viśālākṣī is at Vāraṇasī and Sarasvatī is in Kaśmīra;
these eighteen excellent seats are difficult to attain even for yogins.
One should recite this daily at evening time; it is divine, auspicious, the destroyer of all enemies, the remover of all diseases, and the bestower of all prosperity.
Thus ends the hymn to the eighteen seats of power (śaktipīṭhas).
